record.title: Japan’s energy-conservation regime adds data-centre reporting and a PUE threshold for eligible new builds
record.summary: Japan’s Agency for Natural Resources and Energy (ENECHO) describes additional Energy Conservation Act measures for data-centre operators, including reporting and public disclosure from FY2026 submissions and a PUE≤1.3 standard for eligible new sites from FY2029, assessed after two operating years. Its guidance lists scope thresholds and exclusions. This is an official policy design and reporting obligation; it does not show facility compliance, achieved efficiency, capacity, or AI workload costs.
organizations: Agency for Natural Resources and Energy
Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry of Japan

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ENECHO’s official guidance and FAQ describe FY2026 data-centre reporting and a PUE≤1.3 condition for eligible new sites from FY2029 after two operating years.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The reviewed sources provide policy requirements and reporting descriptions, not measured compliance, achieved efficiency, compute capacity or economic outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: Exact operative text of the amended ordinances and benchmark notification has not been fully compared with ENECHO guidance.
No facility compliance, achieved PUE, energy, cost, or compute impact data are available in the reviewed sources.

brief.importance_rationale: If applied as described, reporting plus a PUE condition changes design and operating constraints for eligible Japanese data centres, with plausible effects on AI-compute siting, energy demand and infrastructure costs. The multi-year lead time, thresholds and exclusions limit scope; no realized costs or efficiency outcomes are established.
limitations: The full operative texts of Ordinance No.81 (26 Dec 2025) and No.59 (1 Jul 2026), plus the separate benchmark notification, were not compared line-by-line with the guidance.
The ENECHO guideline PDF tail was not retrieved; only its first 1,000,000 of 1,219,854 bytes had been inspected in the prior review.

No FY2026 report, compliance, enforcement, achieved PUE, electricity use, project cost, grid/water effect or AI workload economics was inspected. These are not prerequisites for the bounded policy-description claim.
organizations: Agency for Natural Resources and Energy
Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry of Japan
brief.summary: Japan’s Agency for Natural Resources and Energy (ENECHO) describes additional Energy Conservation Act measures for data-centre operators, including reporting and public disclosure from FY2026 submissions and a PUE≤1.3 standard for eligible new sites from FY2029, assessed after two operating years. Its guidance lists scope thresholds and exclusions. This is an official policy design and reporting obligation; it does not show facility compliance, achieved efficiency, capacity, or AI workload costs.

technical.claimed_result: ENECHO says covered operators must report specified data from FY2026 submissions and eligible FY2029 new sites must meet PUE≤1.3 after the two-year operating period.
technical.compute_or_cost: No capex, opex, delivered-power, workload-price or facility-level energy outcome was measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: Official ENECHO guidance and FAQ describe the reporting regime, thresholds and future PUE criterion; this establishes the government’s stated policy, not facility compliance or measured savings.
technical.implementation_status: Official guidance dated 10 Apr 2026 and ENECHO FAQ describe the policy as in force from Apr 2026; detailed final ordinance comparison and enforcement outcomes were not completed.
technical.mechanism: The 2026 guidance adds data-centre energy/PUE reporting to existing energy-conservation submissions and sets PUE≤1.3 for eligible new builds from FY2029 after a two-year operating period, with administrative rationalization-plan steps for underperformance.
technical.novelty: A new sector-specific reporting and future new-build efficiency regime, rather than a measured technology result.
technical.regime: Japan; covered data-centre operators and qualifying facilities under the Energy Conservation Act framework; FY2026 reporting submissions and FY2029+ eligible new builds.
technical.reproducibility: The policy text can be inspected in the original Japanese ENECHO guidance and FAQ; compliance and outcome claims require future reporting and facility data.
technical.strongest_baseline: Before this change, data-centre operators were subject to general energy reporting and a weighted operator-average PUE≤1.4 target for FY2030; the guidance adds facility-level reporting and a separate threshold for eligible new sites.

brief.title: Japan’s energy-conservation regime adds data-centre reporting and a PUE threshold for eligible new builds
brief.why_it_matters: Data-centre energy reporting and a future efficiency condition can affect design, site economics and operating choices for a subset of Japanese compute infrastructure. The public record gives operators several years to adapt, while facility-level costs and effects remain unmeasured.
